output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates did not come from the operators or the printer upgrade. The printer logs show that from 4 Oct the data sent to the printers already carried a 36-month shelf life, and the printed text matched it exactly. No operator override happened on any of the 47 jobs. Thirty earlier jobs, including some after the firmware change and some set up by agency operators, were correct. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value for Veltranol that is only meant to apply from March 2027. The line software appears to have used it early, which contradicts the vendor's statement. We have not explained why. The camera only checks the print against the job data, so it passed every faulty carton.
Next steps: do not discipline or remove the agency operators, and keep the camera check on. Reset the Veltranol shelf-life records. Extend the hold to all Veltranol lots packed since 4 Oct, including the two on Line 1 now in the warehouse. Add a second-person check of the printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Check retained cartons for the two other products whose records carry future-dated changes. Ask the vendor why the future value was used. Whether other products are affected is still unconfirmed, so a 12-month site-wide review and over-labelling are premature.
